score_proposals.evidence_basis: The official environmental statement documents brewing, thermal dealcoholisation, pasteurisation and cleaning-related heat uses and explicitly plans electric clean-steam generation. The company's own programme therefore supports a strong established electric-process-heat fit.

Electric clean-steam generation is an explicit firm-specific process-heat electrification project tied to brewing and cleaning heat demand. This is a clear use case, while multiple separately evidenced electric-process-heat applications are not yet documented.

The 2025 environmental statement documents fossil thermal supply and plans only partial electric clean-steam provision for the KEG plant by end 2026. This supports material substitution potential, not evidence that the entire central thermal service is already replaced.

The official statement documents cooling, refrigeration, pressure-air systems and ventilation together with production/filling processes. These constitute several material compressor, fan and pump/drive applications.

Existing PV requires power conversion and the programme explicitly plans electric clean-steam generation. This supports at least one material firm-specific power-conversion/controlled-heat use case, but not several separately evidenced central converter applications.

The company documents renewed process control and a dated programme to expand process monitoring. Combined with integrated brewing, cooling and utility systems, this supports strong coordinated-control relevance.

Discrete production stages or batch processing support only a weak sequencing hypothesis. The cited source does not establish spare capacity, safe interruption, dispatch permission or a usable shifting window.
Cooled lager tanks and absorption refrigeration do not by themselves establish dispatchable thermal storage. Need a named useful heat/cold buffer and admissible charging/discharging window.

score_proposals.evidence_basis: Electric clean-steam generation is an explicit planned process-heat measure. Replacing part of central thermal service with electric steam would create material additional electrical-load relevance, without estimating kW, MW, MWh or grid capacity.

PV, refrigeration/compressor systems, process control and planned electric clean steam create possible converter/drive-related power-quality relevance, but no direct harmonic, reactive-power, voltage-quality or peak-load issue is documented.

The company documents onsite PV and biogas CHP, with CHP waste heat driving absorption chilling. This is a clear onsite-generation and energy-integration use case; a coordinated microgrid or battery/load-management architecture is not established.
Several concrete measures are documented: PV, biogas CHP with absorption chilling, pressure-air and ventilation heat recovery, fermentation-CO2 recovery and process-control renewal.

The company states EMAS registration since 2025 and long-running ISO 14001 certification, but current independent validity metadata is still unclear and no public ISO 50001 certificate was found. This supports the partial/other-system anchor rather than verified mature-system zero.

The environmental statement documents net greenhouse-gas neutrality by 2045, a 40% reduction target by 2031 from 2021, and dated programme measures through 2026 including electric clean steam, waste-heat use and process monitoring.

The primary 2025 environmental statement documents separate completed investment waves: process-control renewal in 2022–2024, wastewater-biogas/CHP/absorption cooling in 2023, and rooftop PV in 2025. These support several recent projects; the printed PV peak unit is internally suspect and is not used as a rating.

score_proposals.evidence_basis: Official sustainability evidence documents wort processing up to 97 C, predominantly gas-based heat supply and a stated plan to electrify heat supply using heat pumps and solar systems. This supports a strong low-/medium-temperature electrification fit without inferring site load.

The company explicitly plans heat-supply electrification and identifies heat pumps among the intended measures. This is a clear firm-specific use case but does not establish multiple implemented electrification applications.

The report describes heat supply as predominantly gas-based while also documenting substantial brewing and malt-related heat demand and a plan to electrify heat supply. The score reflects substitution potential, not completed displacement.

The official report documents a central refrigeration plant and process operations with cooling demand. This supports material compressor/drive relevance, but the repository evidence does not justify the maximum score for several intensive drive applications.

Planned heat-pump-based heat electrification creates a clear material power-conversion use case. No evidence supports several central converter or rectifier applications, so the maximum anchor is not proposed.
The report documents an operational energy-management system, energy-management software and process-level Power BI reporting, supporting strong sensing and coordinated-control relevance.

Discrete production stages or batch processing support only a weak sequencing hypothesis. The cited source does not establish spare capacity, safe interruption, dispatch permission or a usable shifting window.

Central refrigeration and cooled beer storage do not establish an available thermal buffer for shifting electrical demand. Need a named usable heat/cold store, operating window and quality constraints.

score_proposals.evidence_basis: The company publicly plans electrification of heat supply using heat pumps and other measures. This supports material ordinal new-electric-load relevance without estimating kW, MW, MWh or connection capacity.

Central refrigeration and planned heat-pump electrification make converter-related power-quality effects possible, but the repository contains no direct harmonic, reactive-power, peak-load or voltage-quality evidence.

A 125 kWp PV installation is documented and the company plans additional electrification. This supports a clear onsite-generation integration use case, but no coordinated storage or microgrid deployment is evidenced.

The report documents multiple concrete measures including an operational energy-management system and software, process-level reporting, commissioned PV, solar-thermal activity and prior malt-house modernisation. This is not a no-action case.

Operational energy management and EMAS participation are documented, but no ISO 50001 certificate was found, the available ISO 14001 certificate is expired and current EMAS validity metadata remains unclear. The partial/other-system anchor is therefore proposed.
A quantified 42% Scope 1 and 2 reduction target by 2030 is documented together with a stated heat-electrification direction and planned heat-pump/solar measures.

The 2023 report documents completed rooftop PV in 2023. Solar-thermal installation is beginning/planned; the malt-house energy upgrade is dated only 2021, without a commissioning month inside the strict 2021-10-07 to 2026-10-07 window. Count one safely dated completed project, not planned assets or an unbounded 2021 date.

The validated environmental statement explicitly identifies compressed air, drives, pumps and motors as electricity users and documents a new compressed-air plant. This supports several material drive applications.

The firm documents electrostatic powder coating and electrically driven compressed-air/process equipment. Electrostatic coating provides one clear firm-specific controlled high-voltage/power-conversion use case, but several central converter applications are not established.
